help.title: About Floors
help.overview: A Floor is one level of an edifice. Units sit on a floor. The floor record is the plan layer (name, level number, area, accessibility, shared spaces, media) plus an optional outline on the building plan. It is not a commercial status — units carry available / reserved / sold / rented.

sections.title: What a floor holds
items: Level number — the ordinal of this storey (can be negative for underground).
Accessible / emergency exit flags, description, and a list of shared spaces (lobby, corridor names, and similar labels).
Main image (required) plus optional galleries, videos, extra files, and a marketing booklet.
Optional polygon coordinates — the outline drawn on the edifice plan so the public or panel plan can highlight this floor.
Total units on the floor is computed from children; you do not type it.

sections.title: On this page
items: Opened from an edifice, the list is scoped to that building.
Create a floor, then add units to it. A floor with zero units is valid but will not show inventory.
Open a card to edit plan data and media. Row actions reach units on that floor.
Soft delete can be restored. Units on the floor are not auto-deleted.

sections.title: How it behaves
items: Units must pick a floor (and therefore an edifice and project via cascade).
ROI calculator can narrow by floor when estimating a unit.
The floor is not reserved or sold as a whole — each unit has its own status.

sections.title: Related records
items: Parent: Edifice (which has a Project). Children: Units.
Typical next step: create units with unit type, unit number, areas, rooms, price and currency.
